cover.sub: FDA approves the first factor XIa inhibitor. What it does, and its limits.

visual.name: Asundexian
visual.line: First of its class, FDA, Nov 2026

lines.text: The FDA just approved a brand new class of blood thinner.
Here's what it means, in sixty seconds.
It's called asundexian, and it blocks clotting factor eleven A.

visual.note: The first approved factor XIa inhibitor

lines.text: It's for adults after a recent mild to moderate stroke, or high risk mini stroke.
Stay for fact three. It's the one that matters most.
Fact one. Added to antiplatelets, it cut repeat ischemic strokes by twenty six percent.
Fact two. Major bleeding was similar to placebo, in over twelve thousand patients.
But gut bleeding was more common.
And the big one. It's not approved for atrial fibrillation.
Confirmed: a new option to prevent another stroke.
Still open: how it performs outside trials.
Like and follow Paravion Med for more.

meta.summary: On Nov 9, 2026 the FDA approved asundexian (Sunharbo), the first factor XIa inhibitor, with antiplatelet therapy for adults after a recent mild-to-moderate non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk TIA. In the OCEANIC-STROKE trial it cut ischemic stroke by 26% (relative) with similar major bleeding (1.9% vs 1.7%), but GI bleeding was more common. It is not approved for atrial fibrillation.

removed: Ischemic stroke rates 6.2% vs 8.4%: only found in trade press (TCTMD), not in the FDA release or a trusted source read; cut.
Absolute risk reduction: sources disagree (1.9% at 1 year vs 2.2% at 2 years); cut.
Enrolment number: FDA says 12,327, trade press says 12,237; script says 'over twelve thousand' (Circulation safety population 12,254).
Dose and price: not stated (channel rule: no doses).
meta.notes: News from Nov 9, 2026 (two weeks old): still a top trending topic in neurology/cardiology. Re-check the FDA page and any label update before posting.
meta.verdict: Confirmed: fewer repeat ischemic strokes vs placebo, similar major bleeding. Still open: long-term, real-world performance.
